title: Define SLO credit currency and fallback pricing for multiregion inference
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood routes inference traffic across regions and model variants to meet latency and cost objectives. Current SLO definitions are per-endpoint latency/availability only; we lack a unified mechanism for (1) accounting error-budget consumption in a way that supports cross-region failover and (2) pricing incentives / 'fallback cost' signals that guide automated fallbacks to cheaper model variants without violating customer SLAs.

Goal:
1) Define a compact "SLO credit currency" (error-budget credits) that represents request-quality/duration cost across regions and model variants. Credits should be transfer-friendly across regions and support bounded re-allocation during failover.
2) Define "fallback pricing" rules that attach an explicit credit cost multiplier to model variants/regions used as fallbacks so that the routing layer can make cost-aware failover decisions.
3) Specify measurement and aggregation rules for the per-endpoint SLI surface used to debit/credit the error budget, and operational policies (burn-rate thresholds, probation windows, circuit breaker behavior, eviction-credit reconciliation).

Key deliverables:
- Canonical SLI definitions for this scheme (latency quantiles, availability, quality score for generation routes) and a mapping to credit debits/credits.
- A formal credit accounting model (unit definition, per-request debit formula, rounding and auction semantics during contention).
- Fallback-pricing table and compatibility rules (which variants are eligible, credit multipliers, hard/soft fallback tiers).
- Circuit breaker thresholds and auto-scaling / preemptive-shedding hooks when credit pools approach exhaustion.
- Dashboard and alerting spec: readouts for credit balances, cross-region transfer events, and fallback pricing activations.
- Implementation plan with staged rollout and Canary SLO gates.

SLI & credit model (proposal summary):
- Unit: 1 credit = baseline cost of serving 1 token at model X-base in primary region under median latency.
- Latency SLI: p95 response latency per-route measured over 5m windows, aggregated to 24h rolling windows for SLO compliance checks. Failure = response > latency threshold or 5xx.
- Quality SLI: for generation routes, a lightweight heuristic QA signal (promptset-based sampling) producing a quality score (0..1) per sampled request — sampled at 0.1% by default.
- Debit formula: request_debit = tokens * model_multiplier * region_multiplier * (1 + quality_penalty). Multipliers expressed as scalar decimals (e.g., 0.25 for quantized variant).
- Credit buckets: endpoints have an error-budget bucket expressed in credits (e.g., 1M credits/day). Credits are decremented on SLI-failing events and on expected cost of fallback usage.

Fallback pricing and eligibility: 
- Soft fallback (tier A): variants with compatible tokenizers and no quality-affecting architecture changes, multiplier 1.1-1.5.
- Hard fallback (tier B): faster/quantized variants with known quality delta, multiplier 0.6-0.9 but requires per-tenant opt-in for substantial quality variance.
- Region fallback: cross-region multipliers account for egress and tiered latency tax (e.g., +0.05 per 50ms extra median RTT).
- Pricing table maintained as a CSV in a shared drive and versioned in the config repo.

Circuit breakers, burn-rate and probation: 
- Burn-rate watchpoints: at 3x baseline burn rate => start probabilistic shedding (5%-25%) for non-critical tenants; 5x => hard degrade to tiered soft fallback variants; 8x => regional circuit trip for lowest priority traffic.
- Circuit breaker hysteresis: cool-down 30m after burn rate fall below 1.5x; probation window 2h during which re-entries are limited and traffic is ramped.
- KV-cache affinity: requests that hit the local KV cache consume fewer credits (0.7x) and are preferentially routed. During cache miss storms, prefer regional routing that preserves cache affinity for high-value tenants.

Operational policies and governance: 
- Credits are reconciled hourly. Cross-region transfers allowed up to 10% of daily bucket without manual approval; above that require on-call ops sign-off.
- Emergency escape hatch: PM can temporarily freeze fallback-pricing for a tenant for up to 4h via Console override; all overrides are logged and audited.
- Error-budget replenishment: rolling replenishment at daily boundary; unused credits do not carry over longer than 24h unless explicitly banked by sales/contract.

Rollout plan:
1) Spec approval with Reliability PO and PM (week 0).
2) Implement credit accounting and read-only dashboards in staging (week 1-2).
3) Route simulator & cost-optimizer test harness to validate pricing table (week 3).
4) Canary: enable soft fallback for low-risk internal routes (week 4).
5) Gradual enablement for public traffic behind SLO gates (week 5-7).

Success criteria:
- Credit accounting accuracy within 2% versus batch reconciliation in production during the 7-day canary.
- No >5% regression in end-to-end p95 latency for traffic using fallback variants.
- Alerting correctly fires and prevents automatic promotion of hard fallbacks under low-confidence quality metrics.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should quality SLI be opt-in per tenant due to privacy/regulatory constraints? Proposal: default sampling, with tenant opt-out.
- How aggressive should multipliers be to incentivize cheaper variants without encouraging over-fallback that hurts UX? We propose conservative multipliers for tier A and explicit tenant-level opt-ins for tier B.
- Auditability vs latency: accounting reconciliation must not add measurable latency to the request path; propose an async debit write to the telemetry pipeline with eventual consistency (<= 1s).

Implementation notes / links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://rwd.confluence.com/display/INF/SLO+Credit+Currency+Design
- Pricing table (Drive CSV): https://drive.google.com/example/fallback-pricing.csv
- Prototype PR (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4832
- Dashboard prototype (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood-internal.com/d/credits/credit-accounting

Operational runbook excerpt:
- If credit burn-rate alarm triggers (>=3x sustained for 10m): 1) notify on-call; 2) start 5% probabilistic shedding for non-premium tenants; 3) if burn persists 20m, escalate to failover to soft fallback variants.
- If cross-region transfer >10% of bucket: page SRE lead and hold for manual approval unless in maintenance window.

Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Spec doc reviewed by Reliability, Product, and Solutions Eng
- [ ] Prototype PR merged (read-only telemetry + config parsing)
- [ ] Simulator shows expected cost trade-offs for 3 sample workloads
- [ ] Canary deployment executed and monitoring validated

Notes on related work / dependencies:
- Depends on ENG-712345 (KV cache affinity telemetry shim) and ENG-999999 (tenant-aware SLI taxonomy) for sampling and affinity signals.
